articles.body: French police banned protests in parts of Paris on Thursday as authorities braced for further demonstrations following some of the worst street unrest in years. The restrictions came after President Emmanuel Macron appeared to accuse US President Donald Trump of exploiting the violence for political gain ahead of US midterm elections. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.
articles.headline: Live: Paris bans protests after violent unrest as Macron takes swipe at Trump

articles.body: Russian missiles struck Kyiv overnight, wounding six people and forcing residents into shelters, Ukrainian authorities said Thursday, hours after Moscow signalled readiness to resume US-mediated peace talks. President Donald Trump said negotiations were closer than ever to ending the war, though the Kremlin expressed doubts over Ukrainian and European proposals.
articles.headline: Russian missiles hit Kyiv as Moscow signals readiness for peace talks

articles.body: Irish lawmakers voted Wednesday to scrap a requirement for UN approval before deploying military peacekeepers overseas, approving the controversial legislation by 79 votes to 71. Opposition lawmakers warned the move threatened Ireland’s longstanding military neutrality. Ireland is not a NATO member but has traditionally participated in international peacekeeping missions.
articles.headline: Ireland votes to end UN approval requirement for overseas peacekeeping missions

articles.body: Real Madrid thrashed RB Leipzig 4-1 on Wednesday to secure their third consecutive Champions League victory. Bernardo Silva, Arda Guler, Kylian Mbappé and Yan Diomande scored for Jose Mourinho’s side, while Tidiam Gomis replied for Leipzig. Mbappé has scored in all three European matches this season, taking his tally to 12 goals.
articles.headline: Real Madrid thrash RB Leipzig as Mbappé scores in Champions League win

articles.body: In tonight’s edition: Sudan’s brutal war continues to take a devastating regional toll, as a drone strike in Abyei reportedly kills 153 people. We speak to the UN envoy for Sudan following an emergency international meeting on the escalating crisis. Also, health authorities prepare to coordinate a response as Ebola cases emerge in Nigeria and rise in Kenya. Finally, ten years after Cameroon’s deadliest railway disaster, families of the 79 victims are still fighting for justice, saying their pain has yet to be acknowledged.
articles.headline: Sudan’s war escalates as UN warns of wider regional crisis

articles.body: François Picard welcomes former US Assistant Secretary of Defense Jim Townsend and former US Air Force officer Michael (Mikey) Weinstein, founder and president of the Military Religious Freedom Foundation. Is American military power becoming an instrument of political and religious coercion, both at home and abroad? From the reported restrictions on Ukraine's access to Starlink satellite communications to the Trump administration's overtures towards Vladimir Putin and the growing controversy over religious ideology within the Pentagon, the two guests offer a stark assessment of the direction of American foreign and defence policy.
articles.headline: Trump admin 'destroying' US democracy with 'autocratic, terrorist version of Christian nationalism'

articles.body: Pope Leo XIV, 71, will require no further treatment for lung cancer after tests confirmed the disease was localised, the Vatican said Wednesday. The pontiff underwent surgery last week to remove part of his right lung after being diagnosed with adenocarcinoma. He was discharged Saturday and will gradually resume activities.
articles.headline: Pope Leo XIV needs no further lung cancer treatment, Vatican says

articles.body: Research carried out by the Alliance4Europe NGO suggests that pro-Russian networks manipulated information online in an effort to exacerbate anger in France ahead of last weekend's massive protests and subsequent unrest. After analysing more than half a million posts across various social media platforms, the group says it was able to track the campaign back to the start of September. FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney speaks with Omri Preiss, Managing Director at the Alliance4Europe.
articles.headline: In run-up to mass protests and riots, pro-Russian accounts amplified French anger, NGO finds

articles.body: A New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay $25 billion after a jury found the company deceived users in a case linked to the Cambridge Analytica scandal, media reported Wednesday. The ruling follows an $18 billion settlement with 48 other states over similar claims. Meta called the penalty “a tax on speech".
articles.headline: Meta fined $25 billion in New Mexico over Cambridge Analytica scandal

articles.body: French bond yields have topped 5%, their highest level since 2002, after widespread protests and violence over the weekend. It's a sign that investors are losing confidence in France's finances, as the government grapples with budget and debt problems. Also in the show - chipmaker Nvidia says it's invested $10 billion in European tech firms to boost the 'AI economy,' and the UK approves a controversial natural gas field as PM Andy Burnham faces pressure over energy costs.
articles.headline: French bond yields hit 24-year high after unrest

articles.body: The far-right European Parliament group of French presidential frontrunner Marine Le Pen's party said Wednesday EU prosecutors were searching its offices as part of a graft probe into its now-defunct predecessor. The Patriots for Europe group said the European Public Prosecutor's Office (EPPO) had been searching its administrative offices in Brussels and Strasbourg "since this morning". FRANCE 24's Dave Keating reports from Strasbourg.
articles.headline: EU prosecutors search European Parliament offices of far-right group

articles.body: President ⁠Volodymyr Zelenskiy ​said on Wednesday ​that Ukraine supported a US proposal for ​three-way talks ‌with Russia ⁠and the United ‌States at the level ⁠of negotiators to be held as soon ​as possible, preferably ‌no later than early November. Speaking with FRANCE 24's Mark Owen, Grégoire Roos, Director of the Europe, Russia and Eurasia Programme at Chatham House, says that "it's not clear whether Putin would meet Trump and Zelensky", adding that "meeting Zelensky is the last thing that Putin would be prepared to do".
articles.headline: Putin agrees to resume three-way talks with Kyiv and Washington

articles.body: Donald Trump and his inner circle are using unrest in France to push unsubstantiated claims blaming the riots on immigration, even showing French protest footage at midterm rallies. But there is no evidence linking immigration to the unrest, and it's prompted French President Emmanuel Macron to accuse world leaders of making “stupid comments” at France’s expense. Trump’s focus comes as Republicans face mounting pressure ahead of the midterms and his approval rating hits a reported record low.
articles.headline: Trump exploits France riots to push false immigration claims ahead of midterms

articles.body: The death toll from a drone strike Monday on a market in an area disputed between Sudan and South Sudan has risen to 153 and is likely even higher, a local official told AFP on Wednesday. Authorities in Abyei district said the strike on the Amiet market involved the use of multiple munitions and was carried out by the Sudanese army. FRANCE 24's Mark Owen speaks with Jan Pospisil, Sudan Affairs Analyst at the Peace and Conflict Resolution Evidence Platform. He says that for a long time the Sudanese army has tried "to portray a picture internationally that they are humane, whereas RSF is committing atrocities. Here we see very clearly that there is not much difference between these two".
articles.headline: 'Neither the Sudanese military, nor the RSF take any acknowledgement of human life in this war'

articles.body: Marine Le Pen is set to officially launch her presidential campaign this weekend at the National Rally two-day party congress in Orléans. The latest Ifop poll, carried out in the wake of the mass protests and riots in France, suggests the far right leader would win the first round of the presidential election by a wide margin, and far-left candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon emerged as her most likely opponent in the runoff. FRANCE 24's Emerald Maxwell reports.
articles.headline: Le Pen sees polls boost amid mass protests, riots

articles.body: US President Donald Trump's pivot away from Ukraine has triggered fresh questions about his attachment to Russian leader Vladimir Putin, the man a top American envoy flattered on Wednesday as a "humanitarian. Trump has cast his dealings with Putin as part of a mega-deal that has secured the release of American detainee Stephen Hubbard -- and which Trump says will end Russia's war on Ukraine. FRANCE 24's Gulliver Cragg reports from Kharkiv.
articles.headline: Trump faces fresh questions over ties to 'humanitarian' Putin

articles.body: The Canadian publisher representing Thélyson Orélien on Wednesday said it had dropped the prize-nominated writer over new information indicating that he did use artificial intelligence to write his acclaimed debut.
articles.headline: Canadian publisher drops author Orelien after confirming he used AI in debut novel

articles.body: French President Emmanuel Macron on Wednesday paid an unannounced visit to Riyadh in a bid to underscore French support for the kingdom amid intensified attacks by Houthi rebels and an attempt to ease tensions at home by securing oil and diesel imports.
articles.headline: Macron visits Riyadh to show solidarity amid Houthi attacks, ease tensions at home via fuel deal

articles.body: Inspired by protests in France and other parts of Europe, thousands of Greek students on Wednesday demonstrated around the country.
articles.headline: Greece: Protesters draw inspiration from demonstrations in France

articles.body: The UN is warning that global commitments to cut planet-heating emissions are falling far short of the Paris climate goals of 1.5 degrees Celsius warming – and put the world on course for 2.6C warming this century. The report by the United Nations Environment Programme lays bare the chasm between rhetoric and action when it comes to tackling global warming, and the challenge before political leaders at November's COP31 climate summit - set to take place next month in Turkey. Story by Emerald Maxwell.
articles.headline: World set to breach 1.5°C warming limit set by Paris Climate Agreement

articles.headline: French President Macron lands in Saudi Arabia on surprise 'solidarity' visit

articles.body: Moscow is ready to resume trilateral US-Ukraine-Russia talks next month, the Kremlin said Wednesday after President Vladimir Putin met with US envoy Steve Witkoff in Russia. FRANCE 24's correspondent Gulliver Cragg has more.
articles.headline: Kremlin says 'ready' to resume 3-way talks with US and Ukraine mid-November

articles.headline: Macron rejects Trump’s claims blaming migrants for French riots

articles.body: INTIFADA FLARE UP: One of New York City’s most prestigious public high schools is facing backlash because a school-based socialist youth group co-signed a social media post declaring “Intifada Until Victory!” The Young Democratic Socialists of America chapter of Stuyvesant High School — along with YDSA chapters at Hunter College, the New School, City College and Lehman College — all signed onto an Oct. 8 Instagram post that accused the Democratic Socialists of America’s New York City chapter of silencing student activists who wanted to protest Mayor Zohran Mamdani over Israel. The groups accused the democratic socialist mayor of betraying the Palestinian cause and blasted his decision to keep NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch in her position, referring to her as a “Zionist billionaire.” The term intifada — which refers to violent uprisings against Jews in Israel — is viewed by many Jews as a call to violence against them. Moshe Spern, president of United Jewish Teachers — an advocacy group representing Jewish teachers and students across the city — is demanding the posts be removed immediately and that the YDSA group provide a public apology to the school community. “NYC public schools have seen hundreds of antisemitic and anti-Israel incidents since October 7, 2023,” he wrote in an email yesterday to Stuyvesant Principal Seung Yu and New York City Schools Chancellor Kamar Samuels. “When a school-recognized club amplifies this rhetoric, it risks contributing to a hostile environment.” In the missive, Spern invoked Title VI — the federal law that bans discrimination based on race, shared ancestry and national origin — and demanded a review of the YDSA chapter’s charter, faculty adviser and recent activities for compliance. Spern also cited a chancellor’s regulation that states that student clubs operate under the principal’s supervision and must remain consistent with the school’s educational goals. Yu did not respond to requests for comment. Mamdani’s Department of Education also did not respond to Playbook. Spern told Playbook today that he has yet to receive a response from Yu. “To flat out ignore it is extremely irresponsible,” he said. The NYC-DSA defended the organization. “We support the right to organize,” NYC-DSA co-Chair Gustavo Gordillo said in a statement. “NYC-DSA did not organize or endorse this particular rally, but red scare tactics have never been effective tools for engaging with student movements.” The social media uproar is the latest flashpoint in ongoing tensions in the city over Hamas’ Oct. 7, 2023, attack on Israel and the war that followed. Mamdani, a longtime critic of Israel, was reluctant to condemn the term “globalize the intifada” on the campaign trail last year before finally saying he will not use the term . He also drew bipartisan backlash over his statement marking the third anniversary of the attack. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu labeled the mayor an antisemite , which Mamdani has denied. Mamdani, though, has also simultaneously faced backlash from pro-Palestinian activists who accused him of betraying the Palestinian cause by retaining Tisch, who’s Jewish and a self-described Zionist. Those critics have also criticized him for not doing enough to prevent local synagogues from holding events that promote land sales in Israel, some of them in the occupied West Bank. — Madina Touré From the Capitol Q’S LATEST: Gov. Kathy Hochul has a 55-41 lead over Republican challenger Bruce Blakeman, a Quinnipiac University poll released this afternoon found. That 14-point advantage is narrower than the 19-point lead Quinnipiac gave Hochul last month. But it’s more in line with the numbers from other pollsters: Marist found Hochul up by 11 two weeks ago, Emerson had Hochul up 12 in early October, and Siena measured her lead at 9 points last month. Despite Hochul’s lead, the Q Poll concluded Blakeman has an enthusiasm advantage. A total of 65% of his backers were “very enthusiastic” to support him, while only 33% of Hochul’s supporters said the same. — Bill Mahoney FROM THE CAMPAIGN TRAIL LANDER DETAINED: Democratic congressional candidate Brad Lander was detained today by Israeli security officials while harvesting olives in the West Bank. Lander, a self-described liberal Zionist and critic of Israel , said he went to the West Bank as part of the “Protect the Harvest” coalition to support Palestinians gathering crops. Rabbi Jill Jacobs, CEO of T’ruah, a progressive rabbinical organization, said she was also detained Wednesday, along with “approximately 80 American, Israeli, and international volunteers providing a protective presence for Palestinian farmers.” According to a press release from T’ruah, there were “approximately two hours of peaceful harvesting” until “Israeli forces declared the area a closed military zone” and detained them to transport them to a police station, despite the volunteers agreeing to leave. An Israeli military official told POLITICO that officers from the Israel Defense Forces and Border Police, along with local police, arrived at the scene because Palestinians did not submit a request to coordinate harvesting in that area, which is required ahead of time. The official added that the farm in question “requires only a small number of harvesters to collect its produce” and “the security establishment views the arrival of dozens of activists as an act intended solely to provoke, which undermines the harvesting process.” Lander was released “once the matter was brought to our attention” that he is a congressional candidate, the official said. Lander confirmed in a social media post that he was released with a “warning” because of his “public profile.” Read more from Madison Fernandez in POLITICO . IN OTHER NEWS — MUSK: Elon Musk has spent more than $500,000 to support Rep. Mike Lawler’s reelection bid against Democratic challenger Cait Conley. ( Gothamist ) — STOP: New York City deployed 600 red light cameras to intersections, the maximum number allowed under state law. ( New York Daily News ) — MEASLES: In the wake of a measles crisis, the state Health Department remains locked in a court battle with Amish schools over religious vaccine exemptions. ( The New York Times ) Missed this morning’s New York Playbook? We forgive you. Read it here .

articles.body: Georgia Republicans are counting on Rick Jackson to save them from a wipeout in November — if President Donald Trump doesn’t get in the way. The billionaire health care executive and political newcomer has spent nearly $200 million since he entered the Georgia governor’s race earlier this year. That’s boosted GOP hopes as many in the party have all but given up on the state’s marquee Senate race, where Rep. Mike Collins is struggling to close the gap against a formidably well-funded Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff. Republicans worry that their open contests for attorney general and lieutenant governor as well as control of the state general assembly could be in peril in a larger blue wave. But Jackson’s deep pockets are being tested against a difficult political environment for Republicans, weighed down by unpopular Trump actions, including the war in Iran. And some in the GOP worry that the president’s repeated visits to Georgia could only make the situation worse. “I don't know that Trump coming helps Republicans more so than it excites Democrats, especially in a wave election year, and so becomes and becomes a catch-22 for Republican candidates,” said Jason Shepherd, a former Cobb County chair who is supporting Jackson. One Georgia-based Republican strategist who is not involved in the gubernatorial race posited that Trump’s dual appearances in the state almost certainly did more harm than help. They, like others in this article, were granted anonymity to speak openly about the race to avoid reprisals. “Every piece of data that I've seen, it is not MAGA Republicans that are unmotivated to vote in this election,” the person said. “All the data that I've seen is that the undecideds in our marquee races, and specifically in the governor's race, have a very, very negative opinion of the president. So, I can't really rationalize a case for how it would be helpful.” Jackson, for his part, has carefully navigated his relationship with the president and has not publicly broken with him on policy like other battleground Republicans. But he has not mentioned the president in any of the nearly 150 ads he’s run in the general election, according to an analysis of data from tracking firm AdImpact. Shortly after the RNC announced that Trump would return to the state this weekend, Jackson’s team said in a statement that the candidate will be campaigning in a different part of Georgia. And during his only televised gubernatorial debate on Oct. 6 against Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms, Jackson never name-dropped the president — despite his opponent invoking Trump’s name eight times. Instead, the Republican mentioned popular outgoing GOP Gov. Brian Kemp five times and focused on Bottoms’ tenure as mayor of Atlanta during the Covid-19 pandemic. “It’s been proven time and again that when the message is on Georgia, and the results under Brian Kemp and the conservative vision and road map that's been laid out here, that we win in Georgia. When the focus is on D.C. and personal politics, we lose,” said Cole Muzio, president of the conservative Frontline Policy Action group .  The Jackson campaign declined to comment for this story. “President Trump is the unequivocal leader, best messenger, and unmatched motivator for the Republican Party,” White House spokesperson Davis Ingle said in a statement. Natalie Baldassarre, a spokesperson for the Republican National Committee, said in a statement that Republicans “are laser focused on winning, and our candidates will run the races necessary to best represent their districts and prevent Democrats from taking control." Jackson is one of several Republicans across the country who now must balance between keeping the president close enough to turn out Republican base voters, but not so closely as to alienate the center. Though many Georgia Republicans see Jackson as their de-facto ticket-topper, they don’t see his win as a guarantee against Bottoms, the former Atlanta mayor, in a finicky battleground state like Georgia. Jackson has outspent Bottoms nearly 5-to-1 in the final stretch of the race but still remains in a close race in public polling . And yet, without him, Republicans fear the bottom would have already fallen out on races up and down the ballot, given how poorly Collins is performing in polls against Ossoff. Republicans’ top Senate super PAC, Senate Leadership Fund, was dark in Georgia last week , a sign the race may be slipping out of reach. “If Rick Jackson weren't running, we would all be in a lot of trouble,” said Stephen Lawson, a Georgia-based Republican strategist and Jackson ally. “He’s our best hope at keeping the state red.” A second Georgia-based Republican strategist, who is working on other races in the state, underscored how Jackson’s money is keeping the party afloat. “There is no question in my mind that without the extra $150 million he spent in his general election, that the ticket would be lost,” this person said. “That is the only reason there's still a fight to be had.” But, this person cautioned, the race is still very much a toss-up, and Jackson’s victory will rely on a large share of Georgia voters choosing to split their ballots between Ossoff for Senate and Jackson for governor. Jackson’s allies are optimistic that a significant number of voters will do just that. A private statewide poll reviewed by POLITICO found that roughly 19% of Georgia voters say they are definitely or likely to cast a vote for at least one Democrat and one Republican — a potentially significant pool of crossover voters that could power two very different results in the marquee contests. Whether the sheer force of Jackson’s spending will prove successful enough to overcome Trump is a microcosm of the larger issue his party is experiencing across the country: National Republicans, flush with cash, hold an enormous financial advantage over Democrats. But money alone may not be enough to insulate candidates in battlegrounds or even in traditionally red territory. “I don't know that Republicans across the country should feel as bullish about the cash influx that we've gotten because it didn't work here,” said the first GOP operative. “In terms of actively moving races in our favor, it at least didn't work here.” In the last month, as Bottoms began to spend more heavily on the air amid Jackson's spending advantage, her campaign has noted that polling has started to move marginally in her favor — even if the race remains largely within the margin of error . Her high name ID, as well as cash spent after the primary to define her early, are helping. “Rick Jackson has spent $200 million in this campaign but all the money in the world can’t hide the fact that he would be a lackey for Donald Trump,” TaNisha Cameron, a spokesperson for Bottoms, said in a statement. “Despite being outspent, Keisha’s message is breaking through and she has the momentum in this race right when it matters." Jackson is making more of an effort to tie himself closely to Kemp, who won over moderates and independents in his 2022 reelection for governor and has an approval rating that sits 30 points higher than the president’s in Georgia, according to a recent poll by the Atlanta Journal-Constitution . Kemp, for his part, has continued to be a presence on the trail for Jackson, including joining him on a statewide tour earlier this month and appearing in at least three TV ads for the campaign. But Jackson’s pathway to victory requires him to not only secure crossover voters that may support Ossoff in the Senate race or the type of voters who broke for Kemp, but also turn out the MAGA base who powered the president’s two presidential victories in the perennial battleground. The president is intent on still showing up for him. Shortly after Jackson dispatched Trump’s initially preferred candidate, Lt. Gov. Burt Jones, in June’s primary runoff, the president was quick to praise Jackson as standing “strong with ‘TRUMP.’” And in subsequent posts on Truth Social, Trump has called the health care executive a “good friend.” Trump, onstage Friday, called Jackson a “great businessman,” before adding: “I’ve been watching you, you are good, and he never did this before. He did it because he wants to straighten out things and he’s an amazing, an amazing story.” Aaron Pellish contributed to this report.
articles.headline: Rick Jackson is the GOP’s best hope in Georgia right now

articles.body: Republicans are banking on a massive cash edge to help save their majority in Congress. But they are losing much of that advantage in an important arena: broadcast TV ads. Republicans have spent $677 million on those ads across 10 key Senate battleground states, compared to $479 million by the Democrats. But the GOP’s money isn’t going nearly as far because they’re more dependent on outside groups that pay much higher rates than candidates. The disparity has helped Democrats stay in the fight for Senate control amid an onslaught of GOP outside spending. In Ohio’s Senate race, Republican groups make up 63% of the $218 million spent. But in spite of their nearly 2-to-1 spending advantage over Democrats, they make up just over half of ads that are on the airwaves, according to data from the tracking service AdImpact. In Texas, Republicans have outspent Democrats by a 3-to-1 margin but have aired just 58% of the ads. And in Michigan, the GOP accounts for 60% of the spending but just over half of the ads. A large part of this discrepancy comes down to the mechanics of broadcast advertising. Candidates, and now political parties thanks to a recent Supreme Court ruling, are entitled to significantly lower rates. That has allowed Democratic candidates — who have posted bonkers fundraising hauls — to offset much of the GOP advantage in super PACs. Republican Senate candidates, on the other hand, struggled overall with their fundraising. And some GOP outside groups bought their ad time later, when it was even more expensive. “There are limitations to the impact of ‘big money’ in politics,” said Sean Cooksey, a Republican and former chair of the Federal Election Commission. “It's a good demonstration of the economics of campaign fundraising. Hard dollars really just go so much further.” The disparity also shows “the Republican overreliance on outside groups,” said Ian Russell, a Democratic admaker. “You get an eye-popping dollar amount, but it doesn't actually translate into as many spots as you would think relative to a well-financed candidate,” Russell said. “[Republicans] were just hoping that they could spend their way out of everything that was going wrong for them. But the problem is, their issues run much deeper than a few ad buys can fix. Especially when you've got monster fundraising hauls from the Democratic side.” Republicans in House and Senate races have long been more dependent on outside groups and megadonors, and for multiple cycles have seen their cash advantage undercut by fundraising strength from individual Democratic candidates. But that trend is particularly pronounced this year given the combination of Republican super PAC money and their candidates’ struggles. In 2024, Republican outside groups spent only about 15% more than Democrats on TV ads across House and Senate general election contests, according to a POLITICO analysis of AdImpact data. This cycle, GOP outside groups have spent 7% more. In a few states, the discrepancy between dollars and airtime is less stark. Republicans account for 60% of the spending in Maine’s Senate race and an equal percentage of the ads, according to AdImpact. That’s in part because Sen. Susan Collins has outraised her Democratic opponent Troy Jackson over the whole cycle, although Jackson, who didn’t launch his campaign until July, raised far more in the third quarter. The numbers show the shifting dynamics of campaign strategy after the Supreme Court opened the floodgates to more spending from parties by granting them the lower advertising rate. Republicans have been faster to take advantage of the new rules: Major coordinated spending efforts from the NRSC and RNC have helped their side significantly this cycle. Republicans have far outspent Democrats on Senate party-coordinated Senate advertising, $90 million to $34.6 million across TV, radio and digital ads, according to data from AdImpact. “If I were the leader of either party, I would say you shouldn't give a dollar, you shouldn't give a single penny to these super PACs until you've maxed out to the party committee,” Cooksey said. Some Republicans say that strategic errors have contributed to erasing their cash edge. A number of GOP strategists have also privately griped that MAGA Inc. — one of the major outside groups backing their candidates — bought TV airtime too late, forcing them to pay even higher rates and further draining resources and increasing the price of reaching voters. Republicans fretted for months about whether Trump’s well-financed super PAC, MAGA Inc., would get involved . The group has since spent heavily but only launched its first general election ad buys in September. “There is no question MAGA Inc. should have bought ads earlier in the cycle,” said one national GOP operative who was granted anonymity to discuss party strategy, noting that rates across the country increase as Election Day nears. Other top GOP outside groups, like the Senate Leadership Fund and the Congressional Leadership Fund, made their early advertising reservations much earlier in the cycle than MAGA Inc. Trump allies waved away that criticism. A person familiar with the Trump operation’s midterm planning, granted anonymity to discuss strategy, said it’s "indisputable that the spending from the Trump political effort has kept us competitive in many Senate races.” MAGA Inc. declined to comment. Still, GOP outside groups are utilizing their cash advantage in some underappreciated ways. Republican super PACs have massively outspent their Democratic counterparts on mail — roughly $157 million to $35 million for the general election — according to a POLITICO analysis of independent expenditure filings submitted to the Federal Election Commission. That’s led by a whopping $44 million in spending on mail across 24 races from the Trump-aligned No Going Back PAC, along with $23.8 million across 20 races from Elon Musk’s America PAC. GOP-aligned super PACs have also spent more than Democratic ones on phone calls and text messages, the data shows.

articles.body: BLAKEMAN’S (LACK OF) ENERGY PLAN: GOP gubernatorial candidate Bruce Blakeman continued to hammer Gov. Kathy Hochul on rising energy costs today, promising to slash utility bills in half if he’s elected. The Republican, however, still has not offered up a policy proposal on how he’d go about doing that. “Kathy Hochul increased our utility rates 48 times in four years,” Blakeman said in upper Manhattan this morning. The Washington Heights press conference, which included former Gov. George Pataki, was heavy on rhetoric and relatively light on details. Afterward, Blakeman’s campaign would not spell out how exactly he plans to cut consumer utility costs and did not respond to a request for clarification about his claim that Hochul increased utility rates 48 times. (While the state’s Public Service Commission has approved increases in major utility rate cases during Hochul’s tenure, those hikes have been less than what the utilities requested .) “Donald Trump’s puppet, Bruce Blakeman … wants data centers raising your costs and said Trump was doing an ‘amazing job’ after he jacked up utility bills.” Hochul campaign spokesperson Sarafina Chitika said in a statement. “Two weeks from irrelevance, here’s what Blakeman won’t tell you: Governor Kathy Hochul delivered a billion dollars in energy relief, ten billion in tax relief, and made data centers pay for the energy they use.” The Nassau County executive described meeting the owner of a Bronx diner who told him the business would need to sell 1,000 burgers a month to pay its $16,000 utility bill. Blakeman said he would legalize fracking to help New Yorkers lower their energy bills fast. Aside from the fact that fracking doesn’t necessarily lead to lower utility bills and the reality that Blakeman would need buy-in from the state’s Democratic-dominated Legislature to do so, he insists that legalizing fracking could offer near-term relief from high energy costs. “I met with those same individuals and companies that are doing the extraction of natural gas in Pennsylvania. They told me they can be up and running in 60 days,” Blakeman said. “If Albany has the will to reduce people's utility bills … we can get it done in 60 days.” He pointed to Pennsylvania, arguing that the state has lower electric bills because it allows fracking. But he neglected to mention that Pennsylvania is not part of the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative — the carbon trading program of 11 eastern states, which Blakeman has pledged to withdraw from if he is elected. Pataki, the last Republican to serve as governor in the Empire State, spearheaded the creation of that initiative, which is commonly known as RGGI. “The concept is right, but the way it's being done in Albany is wrong,” Pataki said at the presser, accusing Albany of using RGGI as a “slush fund.” Even if New York did withdraw from RGGI, the benefit would amount to a 5% to 6% decrease on an average New York residential household bill, according to an estimate from National Grid — barely making a dent in the 50% Blakeman is promising to slash. Exactly how the state would cover the rest of his proposed cut remains unclear. Affordability, though, continues to be a key concern in Washington Heights, a largely Dominican neighborhood that Mayor Zohran Mamdani did well in during his ascent to victory last year. To drive their message home, the Republicans even attempted to make their pitch in Spanish. Pataki, much more practiced in this than Blakeman, talked about how much he loved the “barrio” when he was governor, describing Blakeman as a leader “muy fuerte.” “Gracias, hombre grande,” Blakeman exclaimed, before touting what he views as the GOP ticket’s immigrant bonafides — Saritha Komatireddy for attorney general and Joe Hernandez for comptroller. “Governor, your Spanish is better than my Spanish, and I grew up speaking it,” Hernandez praised Pataki. — Mona Zhang From the Capitol LABOR BOOSTS GOV: A coalition of public employee unions is joining the crowded roster of super PACs spending on the gubernatorial election. The New York Accountability Coalition has received $550,000 in recent weeks from the Civil Service Employees Association, Public Employees Federation, District Council 37, and CWA District One. It’ll soon spend that money to boost Hochul. The governor “is laser-focused on lowering costs for working families and investing in public services,” AFSCME’s Courtney Brunelle-Kim said. “Bruce Blakeman is just another pay-to-play politician. From now until Election Day, we’ll be working to ensure that voters in key districts know The Blakeman Record.” The super PAC spent $460,000 this spring helping Comptroller Tom DiNapoli as he faced two Democratic primary challengers. — Bill Mahoney FROM THE CAMPAIGN TRAIL AD PULLED: A clean energy super PAC yanked a version of an ad airing in a competitive upstate House district after Republican candidate Anthony Constantino’s attorney complained the spot was defamatory. The group Invest In Tomorrow Coalition recently began airing the spot in the sprawling North Country House seat that accused Constantino — who runs a custom sticker business — of selling anti-police merchandise. “What do Anthony Constantino and violent anti-cop extremists have in common? They both think ‘kill the police’ is a good slogan,” the ad’s narrator says. Constantino’s attorney last week contacted a lawyer for the super PAC alleging the contents of the ad were false and defamatory. On Saturday, the group signaled it would suspend further distribution of the current ad. So far, the PAC has spent some $243,000 in the district in the last three days, according to AdImpact. “Anthony Constantino may lawyer up, but he can’t sticker over the truth: he’s gotten rich off selling vile merch, including hosting a listing for a ‘Kill the Police’ sticker and other anti-cop listings that are still active today ,” said Chris Coffey, a spokesperson for the group. “As a token of our gratitude and recognition of his desire to spread that message, ITC PAC is putting $250,000 more behind the original ad buy to make sure all of NY-21 knows the real Anthony Constantino.” The fight over the commercial comes as Constantino is trying to retain the seat being vacated by GOP Rep. Elise Stefanik. Polls have shown Democrat Blake Gendebien running competitively against the Republican, however, giving the race a surprising dose of uncertainty in the final two weeks. — Nick Reisman HOUSE HUNTING: Two New York battleground districts have again moved in Democrats’ favor, according to a nonpartisan election forecaster. Sabato’s Crystal Ball shifted Stefanik’s upstate seat from “likely Republican” to “leans Republican” today, as well as Democratic Rep. Laura Gillen’s Long Island district from “leans Democratic” to “likely Democratic.” The Stefanik seat covers a sprawling, deep-red area — though Democrats are feeling bullish in part because of the Trump administration’s tariffs impacting farmers there. Gillen faces a challenge from Hempstead Receiver of Taxes Jeanine Driscoll. Kamala Harris narrowly won that district in 2024, but Republicans are counting on tailwinds from Blakeman, the Nassau County executive, to boost down-ballot candidates. — Madison Fernandez IN OTHER NEWS — REAL ESTATE STRIKES BACK: A new organization called Built For New York hopes to promote the real estate industry’s interests in the wake of a pro-tenant political sweep in New York City. ( The New York Times ) — PAC ALERT: A coalition of Jewish Democrats from the Capital Region launched a state-level PAC dedicated to supporting liberal candidates who push back on anti-Jewish and anti-Israel forces. ( Jewish Insider ) — BOOZE BUCKS: Lily Fan, chair of the State Liquor Authority and a close Hochul ally, donated $40,000 to a pro-Hochul super PAC that’s run by people who lobby the liquor industry. Díaz, pudiera darle la noticia, el único ciudadano español nacionalizado al amparo de la <i>ley de nietos</i> que acudió al Tribunal Constitucional para adherirse al recurso de amparo del Defensor del Pueblo ya le había enviado el enlace de la información con el fallo. El pleno del tribunal de garantías había inadmitido, por diez votos a dos, <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-21/el-constitucional-rechaza-el-amparo-por-la-ley-de-nietos-con-el-voto-en-contra-de-dos-magistrados-progresistas.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-21/el-constitucional-rechaza-el-amparo-por-la-ley-de-nietos-con-el-voto-en-contra-de-dos-magistrados-progresistas.html">el recurso que reclamaba restablecer el derecho al voto</a> de más de 160.000 nacionalizados, entre ellos el suyo. Junto al enlace, el hombre, español de origen argentino, escribió una pregunta tan breve como cargada de desazón: “¿Y ahora qué se puede hacer?”. El portazo judicial lo dejó triste y desmoralizado, aunque no ha conseguido apagar del todo su esperanza. Su abogado, sin embargo, mira al futuro con mucho menos optimismo. Las posibilidades de que los afectados puedan votar el próximo 29 de noviembre son, a su juicio, “pocas o ninguna”.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-10-22/el-abogado-de-afectados-por-la-ley-de-nietos-asume-que-no-podran-votar-el-constitucional-era-la-unica-via-posible.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <p>La retirada del derecho al voto a más de 160.000 nacionalizados por la llamada <i>ley de nietos</i> ha puesto el foco en una ley y una instrucción aprobadas en octubre de 2022 sin que ningún partido político las recurriera. La <a href="https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2022-17099" target="_self" rel="" title="https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2022-17099">Ley de Memoria democrática se publicó en el Boletín Oficial del Estado (BOE)</a> el 19 octubre de ese año tras un año de compleja tramitación parlamentaria con intensos debates, no solo entre el Gobierno y la oposición sino también con los socios de investidura. La <a href="https://www.boe.es/diario_boe/txt.php?id=BOE-A-2022-17470" target="_self" rel="" title="https://www.boe.es/diario_boe/txt.php?id=BOE-A-2022-17470">instrucción del Ministerio de Justicia con las directrices</a> para tramitar el derecho a optar a la nacionalidad española se aprobó seis días después y solo fue impugnada por una asociación contraria a las leyes de memoria histórica y democrática, pero su recurso fue desestimado por una cuestión de forma. Cuatro años después, el debate político a las puertas de un nuevo ciclo electoral ha desenterrado aquella instrucción que en su momento pasó inadvertida para los partidos y ahora ha derivado en un enorme embrollo jurídico.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-10-22/que-dice-la-instruccion-de-la-ley-de-nietos-que-esta-bajo-la-lupa-del-supremo.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <p>No es la primera vez que sucede. Hace dos años, en junio de 2024, en la anterior visita de Javier Milei a España, Isabel Díaz Ayuso incomodó a Génova <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2024-06-19/ayuso-condecorara-a-milei-quien-vuelve-a-insultar-a-sanchez-antes-de-viajar-a-madrid-llamandolo-cobarde.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2024-06-19/ayuso-condecorara-a-milei-quien-vuelve-a-insultar-a-sanchez-antes-de-viajar-a-madrid-llamandolo-cobarde.html">al otorgar al presidente de Argentina la medalla internacional de la Comunidad de Madrid,</a> en un acto con toda la pompa del que fue ajeno el líder del PP. Ahora, en plena precampaña electoral, la presencia del histriónico mandatario latinoamericano vuelve a ser incómoda para el PP, salvo para la presidenta de la Comunidad de Madrid, que ha vuelto a reivindicarlo como un referente, al recibirlo calurosamente y exhibir complicidad con un abrazo mientras el líder de su partido lo ignoraba y ponía tierra de por medio con un acto en Sevilla centrado en las políticas de vivienda. Los populares son conscientes de que los insultos de Milei en Madrid a Pedro Sánchez, a quien llamó este miércoles “impresentable dictador”, pueden activar al electorado progresista, pero confían en que el impacto de la visita del presidente argentino se diluya porque aún faltan 40 días para la cita con las urnas. “Menos mal que ha venido ahora y no el 21 de noviembre, porque si llega a venir la última semana de campaña el escenario sería distinto”, admite un dirigente. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-22/el-pp-confia-en-que-el-impacto-de-la-visita-de-milei-se-diluya-el-29-n-si-llega-a-venir-la-ultima-semana-seria-distinto.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <p><a href="https://elpais.com/videos/2026-10-21/el-paso-de-javier-milei-por-madrid.html?autoplay=1" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/videos/2026-10-21/el-paso-de-javier-milei-por-madrid.html?autoplay=1">Javier Milei</a> le ha puesto en bandeja otra semana de campaña a Pedro Sánchez. El presidente del Gobierno, que ya el lunes señaló a la motosierra del presidente argentino como el modelo de recortes públicos a seguir por PP y Vox si gobiernan, no ha desperdiciado lo que considera un regalo en la antesala de las elecciones generales. “Si sus amigos Feijóo y <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-21/milei-a-abascal-en-una-videollamada-para-mi-es-un-placer-patear-culos-zurdos.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-21/milei-a-abascal-en-una-videollamada-para-mi-es-un-placer-patear-culos-zurdos.html">Abascal </a>ganan las elecciones y gobiernan, van a hacer en España lo mismo que Milei hace en Argentina”, ha advertido Sánchez en Burgos en el sexto mitin desde que convocó el adelanto electoral. La mitad han sido en Castilla y León, una comunidad prioritaria en la estrategia del PSOE, donde cada día están más seguros de que pueden ganar las elecciones a un PP estancado incapaz de contener a Vox. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-10-21/sanchez-azuza-el-miedo-a-la-motosierra-de-milei-si-feijoo-y-abascal-gobiernan-van-a-hacer-en-espana-lo-mismo-que-en-argentina.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <p>El Tribunal Constitucional <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-21/el-constitucional-rechaza-el-amparo-por-la-ley-de-nietos-con-el-voto-en-contra-de-dos-magistrados-progresistas.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-21/el-constitucional-rechaza-el-amparo-por-la-ley-de-nietos-con-el-voto-en-contra-de-dos-magistrados-progresistas.html">ha inadmitido este miércoles el recurso del Defensor del Pueblo</a> contra la suspensión, por orden del Tribunal Supremo, del derecho al voto de 160.000 españoles nacionalizados <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-10-21/tras-la-decision-del-constitucional-sobre-la-ley-de-nietos-sigue-suspendido-el-voto-podran-participar-el-29-n.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-10-21/tras-la-decision-del-constitucional-sobre-la-ley-de-nietos-sigue-suspendido-el-voto-podran-participar-el-29-n.html">en virtud de la <i>ley de nietos. </i></a>Dada la relevancia del asunto, y contra la costumbre del órgano de garantías, que suele despachar las inadmisiones con providencias de un par de líneas, esta vez ha dictado un auto para explicar su decisión de inadmitir el recurso del Defensor por “prematuro”, puesto que no se han agotado la vía judicial ordinaria: “El Tribunal Supremo ha de pronunciarse nuevamente, a la vista de las alegaciones de las partes que comparezcan″, afirma el auto, redactado por el magistrado Enrique Arnaldo, en referencia al plazo de alegaciones abierto para que los afectados por la suspensión puedan personarse. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-21/los-argumentos-del-constitucional-sobre-el-recurso-de-la-ley-de-nietos-la-ineficacia-administrativa-no-sirve-de-fundamento-para-admitir-un-amparo.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <img src="https://imagenes.elpais.com/resizer/v2/3HXQF4HF35HKDEZNCYTIQZCSV4.jpg?auth=7d26d677848bd164f9af18fec52f421343f524d8dd5089e1415c4f9db57bfeec" width="2500" height="1667" alt="El alcalde de Estepona (Málaga), José María García Urbano, en una imagen de archivo."></img><p>La Fiscalía de Marbella ha solicitado un año y 11 meses de prisión para el alcalde de Estepona (Málaga, 78.413 habitantes), <a href="https://elpais.com/noticias/jose-maria-garcia-urbano/" rel="">José María García Urbano</a> (PP) al que acusa de <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2025-04-30/el-alcalde-de-estepona-ira-a-juicio-acusado-de-malversacion-de-caudales-en-la-contratacion-de-una-amiga-intima-como-asesora.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2025-04-30/el-alcalde-de-estepona-ira-a-juicio-acusado-de-malversacion-de-caudales-en-la-contratacion-de-una-amiga-intima-como-asesora.html">un delito de prevaricación y otro de malversación de caudales.</a> La fiscal Alejandra Gómez pide la apertura de juicio oral y sostiene su petición argumentando que el regidor, que lleva en el cargo desde el año 2011, contrató como cargo de confianza municipal a una mujer con la que mantenía una relación sentimental “a sabiendas de que no iba a desempeñar actividad laboral alguna” y que, a pesar de ello, esta cobró algo más de 5.000 euros. El ministerio público también pide para García Urbano cinco años de inhabilitación como cargo o empleo público.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-21/la-fiscalia-pide-un-ano-y-11-meses-de-prision-para-el-alcalde-de-estepona-por-prevaricacion-y-malversacion.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: L’habitatge ha tornat a centrar bona part del discurs del síndic de greuges de Barcelona, David Bondia, que ha advertit a l’ Infobarris que ha proposat una compra col·laborativa del Bloc Papallona , a la Nova Esquerra de l’Eixample. El síndic que ha mediat entre el veïnat, les entitats socials, la propietat i l’Ajuntament ha assegurat que hi ha diverses propostes sobre la taula , com ara la compra dels immobles per part d’entitats vinculades a l’habitatge o la seva incorporació a la borsa de lloguer social. Ha estat contundent en proposar una actuació d’urgència: “ Fer taxacions dels blocs i veure què pot passar, si pot ser una compra col·laborativa, si poden entitats del sector de l’habitatge comprar aquests blocs i si poden entrar a la borsa de lloguer social”. La proposta arriba després que el tinent d’alcaldia d’Economia, Hisenda, Promoció Econòmica i Turisme, Jordi Valls, anunciés que “l’Ajuntament no ho ha de comprar tot” i que cal explorar altres fórmules que permetin als veïns continuar vivint als seus habitatges. També et pot interessar Vaga de lloguers al Bloc Papallona: els veïns reclamen la renovació dels contractes Francis Manzano Rojas Maria Solans 2 minuts de lectura “Sense habitatges no hi ha drets socials” Segons Bondia, la pressió dels moviments socials ha contribuït a fer replantejar algunes pràctiques dels fons d’inversió i ha reclamat mantenir obertes les vies de diàleg per evitar l’expulsió de veïns dels barris: “La ciutat necessita un canvi de model perquè garantir l’accés a un habitatge digne és la base de molts altres drets. Sense habitatge no hi drets socials” . El síndic, que acaba de renovar el càrrec , ha defensat més inversió en habitatge públic, una millor gestió del parc municipal i l’acceleració de la rehabilitació d’edificis amb problemes estructurals en barris com el Besòs, el Maresme i la Trinitat Vella. A més, Bondia ha destacat la necessitat de recuperar pisos buits per a ús residencial i social , una realitat que, segons ha constatat en les seves visites als barris, és especialment visible a Gràcia on un equip de betevé ha estat testimoni de la trobada. A Collserola “les restriccions han de ser l’excepció” També s’ha referit a la crisi de la pesta porcina i el tancament de Collserola. El síndic ha sentenciat que les ajudes econòmiques per establiments que acreditin pèrdues superiors al 30 % “ arriben molt tard i s’haurien d’haver previst abans “. No es cobraran fins al febrer del 2027 perquè hauran de tancar el comptes d’aquest any per comptabilitzar les pèrdues i, mentrestant, Bondia ha subratllat que molts hauran de fer acomiadaments. De fet, pel camí han tancat comerços. El síndic ha demanat que es creïn itineraris segurs, perquè “ la limitació (de circulació) no sigui la regla, sinó sigui l’excepció “. Ha apostat per prohibir només l’accés en zones on estigui acreditat que hi ha el virus, “però reobrir camins en zones epidemiològiques segures. S’ha de prevenir, però també el que podem fer és limitar la zona de restricció”, ha considerat Bondia, i ha lamentat que estem massa acostumats a mesures de caràcter general. Reclama que s’acotin on estigui el brot. Unes declaracions que arriben després que l’Ajuntament ha anunciat la reobertura esglaonada de Collserola i prioritza la carretera de les Aigües. articles.body: (ACN) L’Ajuntament de Barcelona ja està preparant una proposta per treballar sobre les zones de Collserola que es podrien començar a desescalar quan es reobri el parc natural a finals d’any, com va anunciar diumenge el conseller d’Agricultura, Òscar Ordeig . La intenció del consistori és fer-ho en funció del risc i mantenint els criteris de seguretat que es considerin oportuns per la crisi de la pesta porcina . Sobre la desescalada, una de les zones que l’Ajuntament vol reclamar que s’obri és la carretera de les Aigües , segons ha dit el tinent d’alcaldia de Seguretat, Albert Batlle , a la Comissió d’Ecologia, Urbanisme, Mobilitat i Habitatge. “Des de l’Ajuntament ja estem preparant una proposta per elevar-la a la conselleria”, ha dit Batlle. El Parc de Collserola està tancat des de fa set mesos , quan es va detectar el primer cas d’un senglar infectat per la pesta porcina a la ciutat. També et pot interessar El govern preveu reobrir Collserola a finals d’any “amb corredors segurs” Núria Granados 1 minut de lectura Batlle recorda que cal ser prudents Batlle s’ha remès a les declaracions del mateix conseller Òscar Ordeig del cap de setmana i ha recordat que la Generalitat ha creat un grup tècnic i una taula de coordinació política per començar a treballar les zones de Collserola que es podrien desescalar de forma gradual. Tot i això, ha recordat que les decisions responen a condicions tècniques i científiques d’acord amb els protocols i amb la normativa europea. “Decisions que tots hem de respectar perquè ens hi juguem conseqüències econòmiques molt greus per al país, pèrdua de mercats internacionals, restriccions comercials i un impacte sever sobre el sector”, ha apuntat. Així, ha demanat mantenir la prudència tot i reconèixer que són molt conscients de les molèsties que suposen les restriccions de Collserola . També et pot interessar Veïns del Parc de Collserola reclamen que reobri per salut mental: “Alguns tenim ansietat” Jordi Escofet 2 minuts de lectura Celebració amb alguns “peròs” Veïns i comerciants de la zona han celebrat el comunicat, tot i que amb reserves per la repercussió que han tingut aquests mesos de tancament. Mentre el veïnat apunta que és una gran notícia per reprendre l’oci a la natura, els comerciants alerten que fa mesos que pateixen les conseqüències del tancament: “Ara podrem treballar novembre i desembre, però això no compensa els darrers 10 mesos”, apunta Sílvia Baldellou, de l’Associació de Comerciants de Vallvidrera. En aquest sentit, expliquen, acumulen moltes pèrdues i que els ingressos han baixat entre un 10 i un 15 %.

articles.body: La XI edició del Summit Barcelona Oberta ha servit per posar blanc sobre negre als acords i desacords que aquesta entitat —que agrupa 24 eixos comercials— manté amb les polítiques de l’Ajuntament de Barcelona en alguns camps. Els lloguers comercials en són un exemple. L’alcalde de Barcelona, Jaume Collboni , ha anat al gra a l’hora de posar el tema sobre la taula: “Cal obrir el debat sobre la regulació dels lloguers comercials , especialment en la successió de contractes amb algunes pujades que han expulsat el comerç tradicional del barri “, ha dit en la primera intervenció de l’acte. I poc després Barcelona Oberta ha reiterat que no hi estan d’acord. Ben al contrari, ho emmarquen en el que qualifiquen d’excés d’intervencionisme de les administracions, i ho equiparen a la xarxa de supermercats públics , que també rebutgen. L’XI Summit de Barcelona Oberta ha portat per nom ‘La Barcelona que podria ser’ i ha servit a l’entitat per reclamar a les administracions “que facilitin l’activitat econòmica i es deixi de posar traves al comerç”. En aquest sentit, demanen millorar l’accessibilitat, flexibilitzar els plans d’usos, més agilitat administrativa i poder obrir els diumenges , una reivindicació històrica de l’entitat. També diferents eixos comercials hi han expressat les seves inquietuds i peticions. Crit d’auxili de Ciutat Vella Especialment preocupats s’han mostrat des de Barnacentre , que lamenten la pèrdua de diversitat comercial a Ciutat Vella . “Hem perdut la gran majoria del nostre comerç. Com el portarem una altra vegada?”, ha exclamat Núria Raja. I ha llançat un dard també per la mobilitat: “El tema de la mobilitat el tenim molt espatllat, i a Ciutat Vella no ens arriben els clients, els amics i la gent que necessitem. Hi ha molt turista, però volem la gent de casa”, ha etzibat. Teresa Guirado de Diagonal Boulevard ha expressat el temor per quan arribin les obres de la connexió del tramvia fins a Francesc Macià . “Necessitem informació, previsió i interlocució sobre una infraestructura com aquesta”. I per això, reclamen conèixer el projecte amb antelació, el calendari i les afectacions als accessos. Proposen, de fet, crear una taula i ser-hi presents per poder estar al cas de tot i dir-hi la seva. Des de Gaudí Shopping celebren que es posi fil a l’agulla a la reforma de l’avinguda de Gaudí. L’ Eix Pelai espera que es faci realitat la rehabilitació que ha de convertir el carrer en un bulevard . I des d’ Amics de la Rambla , Fermín Villar ha recordat que “la Rambla recull i genera molta taxa turística i seria de justícia que se li retorni”. També han expressat les seves inquietuds altres entitats com Som Sant Antoni , Born Comerç i els comerciants de la plaça Reial . “Comprar és com votar” A la trobada tothom ha estat d’acord que el comerç local forma part de la identitat de la ciutat. I que no només es tracta de negocis que generen llocs de treball i ingressos fiscals, sinó també d’una xarxa que proporciona cohesió, seguretat i dinamització als barris. És prioritari, coincideix tothom, preservar-ho, però “per moltes polítiques públiques que fem, si la gent no va a comprar a la botiga del barri això no val”, ha recordat Collboni. “Comprar és com votar”, ha dit l’alcalde, “perquè decidir on comprar és decidir quina ciutat estem fent. Si compro aquí o allà, estic determinant quin tipus d’economia i comerç tindré al meu barri”. Pel que fa a Barcelona Oberta, el president, Gabriel Jené, ha expressat la voluntat del sector de participar en les solucions i ha demanat convertir les reflexions del Summit en decisions, acords i millores visibles als carrers.

articles.body: L’onada de protestes contra l’encariment de la vida s’estén ja per Europa . Itàlia, Bèlgica, Portugal i Albània són alguns dels molts països que des de fa setmanes viuen actes de protesta generades pel malestar social, però les imatges més impactants d’aquest cap de setmana s’han viscut a França , agreujades pels saqueigs i la crema de mobiliari urbà . La violència ha escalat en les últimes protestes, un dels incidents més destacats ha estat l’incendi provocat pels manifestants a l’ajuntament de Llemotges. L’especialista en relacions i política internacional i professor associat a la UB, Jesús Maestro, ha apel·lat en una entrevista al programa bàsics , de betevé, al “desencís” dels joves. “Vull creure que hi ha una part de rebel·lia autèntica, més enllà dels aldarulls , en aquestes protestes”. Maestro afirma que és una situació que ve de lluny. “Volem una millor educació, sous més dignes i veuen que aquells qui manen no responen a les seves demandes”, ha detallat l’expert, qui ha assegurat que això només pot tenir dues derivades : “Una reforma radical del sistema, que és complicada, o una situació de col·lapse polític, social i econòmic”. També et pot interessar Mobilització massiva a Barcelona pel dret a l’habitatge: “Volem que la vaga sigui un èxit” Marina Segura i Vidal 2 minuts de lectura “Els joves francesos no tenen present” Pel que fa a la situació a França, Maestro ha fet referència al deteriorament de l’estat de benestar , especialment a sectors més populars. Tot i que les protestes no són alienes a la resta del món, l’expert explica que hi ha diversos motius que són “estrictament francesos ” com per exemple l’envelliment de la població, les retallades en educació, cultura i serveis socials i l’augment dels preus del carburants arran de la guerra amb l’Iran, una situació “molt complicada des de fa dècades”. “ No és que els joves no tinguin futur, és que no tenen present “, ha afirmat Moreno, contundent. També et pot interessar CCOO i UGT acorden convocar una vaga general a la tardor pel dret a l’habitatge Jessica Moreno Cusac 1 minut de lectura “Els partits tradicionals s’han allunyat del que vol la ciutadania” L’expert explica que aquesta situació forma part d’un “ caldo de cultiu que afavoreix els discursos extrems, especialment el de l’extrema dreta “. “El ciutadà mitjà de França el que veu és que li cremen l’ajuntament i saquegen les botigues”, ha detallat l’expert, que afegeix que qui sempre dona respostes fàcils a problemes complexos són “el populisme i l’extrema dreta”. És per aquest motiu que Maestro ha afirmat que qui sortirà afavorit de tot plegat serà “el nacionalisme més extrem . La seva resposta és allargar el conflicte i no fer aflorar els problemes de fons”. “ Els partits tradicionals s’han allunyat d’allò que vol la ciutadania “, ha conclòs. articles.body: La previsió del temps per a aquest dijous, 22 d’octubre, anuncia un increment destacable dels núvols . El sol brillarà amb poca força, especialment al matí on la nuvolositat serà densa i compacta . Fins al migdia hi haurà risc d’algun ruixat aïllat més probable a la façana marítima. Descens lleuger de la temperatura. Tenim 20 ºC al Poblenou i un 62 % d'humitat. Amb el pas de les hores, els núvols augmentaran arreu de l'entorn metropolità. Més enllà de mig matí, la nuvolositat tendirà a trencar-se, però el trànsit de núvols alts i prims s’assegurarà que tinguem un cel blanquinós i enteranyinat . Temperatura semblant o més baixa. Les màximes difícilment superaran els 20 ºC , tot i que s’hi acostaran molt, en la majoria de barris rondaran els 17 i 19 ºC. En termes generals s’espera una recta final de setmana variable, núvols i sol, sense descartar alguns xàfecs passatgers entre el vespre de divendres i dissabte. Més endavant, la temperatura podria recuperar-se una mica i deixar-nos un ambient més suau , però això no vol dir que hagi de fer calor . articles.body: L’ Asian Film Festival Barcelona arrencarà aquest dijous i s’allargarà fins a l’1 de novembre. Es podran veure més de 100 obres de cinema asiàtic actual de 25 països , amb especial focus a les produccions de l’Índia . Organitzat per Casa Asia , el festival arriba a la 14a edició i ofereix el cinema més actual tant de directors consolidats i emergents , i en camí de consolidar-se com un aparador internacional de referència per al cinema asiàtic. Cinema de plena actualitat de 25 països asiàtics El festival ha programat més d’un centenar de pel·lícules representatives del cinema independent, experimental i d’autor , produïdes majoritàriament entre 2025 i 2026 , que ens acosta a la realitat d’aquestes geografies. Es podran veure produccions de l’Àsia central, l’Àsia meridional, el sud-est Asiàtic, l’Àsia oriental i la regió Àsia-Pacífic. Des de filmografies emergents en països com Kazakhstan, Mongòlia, Nepal, Sri Lanka, el Pakistan, Afganistan i Cambodja com a produccions de grans indústries com l’Iran i la Xina. També hi haurà un tast de títols procedents de Hong Kong, Indonèsia, Singapur, Malàisia, Tailàndia i Vietnam, així com d’Austràlia i Nova Zelanda. Fotograma de No good men (2026), de Shahrbanoo Sadat. També et pot interessar De supermercat a cinema i no al revés: els Verdi estrenen dues sales el proper desembre Esther Castarnado 1 minut de lectura Entre les destacades, No good men (2026), dirigida per la cineasta afganesa Shahrbanoo Sadat . L’autora interpreta Naru, l’única operadora de càmera de Kabul News . Just abans de l’entrada al poder dels talibans , la periodista lluita per mantenir la custòdia del seu fill. I també Kurak (2025), d’ Erke Dzhumakmatova , que narra la història d’una jove model que que cau en el xantatge d’un agent de policia, en paral·lel a una mare que busca justícia per a la seva filla , que es va treure la vida després de ser violada, tot això en un context de violència real al Kirguizstan. Fotograma de Kurak (2025), d’Erke Dzhumakmatova. Focus especial al cinema de l’Índia A més de la pel·lícula inaugural If on a winter’s night (2025), el segon llargmetratge del director i guionista indi Sanju Surendra , el festival ha programat 12 llargmetratges de directors indis realitzats entre el 2025 i el 2026. Fotograma de If on a winter’s night (2025), de Sanju Surendra. La selecció permet endinsar-se en la diversitat del cinema independent contemporani d’aquesta gran potència cinematogràfica. La tria inclou des de noms consolidats, com el de Rima Das , amb Not a hero (2026), a veus emergents com Laksmipriya Devi , amb Boong (2024), i Omkar Bhatkar , amb Iktsuarpok (2026), representants d’un cinema allunyat del model de Bollywood que explora narratives i llenguatges visuals que ens endinsen en les transformacions socials i culturals de l’Índia actual . Fotograma d’ Iktsuarpok (2026), d’Omkar Bhatkar. A aquestes pel·lícules, cal afegir-hi la retrospectiva de 12 títols més que ens acosten a la mirada occidental de l’Índia , amb produccions fetes entre 1946 i 2023 . A Barcelona, la seu principal de les projeccions serà els Cinemes Girona però també hi ha programades sessions a CaixaForum Barcelona, Zumzeig, Fundació Institut Confuci Barcelona, Soho House i l’Escola de Cinema de Barcelona. articles.body: betevé ha signat un acord de col·laboració amb Barcelona de Serveis Municipals (B:SM) que ha permès la instal·lació de dues càmeres d’alta definició que serviran especialment per fer seguiment del temps a casa nostra sense tenir cap zona sense cobrir . També et pot interessar La previsió del temps per a Barcelona, actualitzada La del Port Olímpic, la vista cap el sud Aquestes càmeres se sumen a la ja existent, situada al Castell de Montjuïc, que ja oferia una vista preciosa de la ciutat de Barcelona, especialment mirant cap el nord. Ara, la càmera instal·lada a la torre de capitania del Port Olímpic permetrà saber què passa també mirant cap al sud . Aquesta càmera ens mostra una silueta de la ciutat força desconeguda per a molts barcelonins i ens permet veure la bocana de sortida del Port Olímpic , però també una imatge preciosa de les dues torres bessones amb el Tibidabo al fons . La càmera del Port Olímpic servirà per veure amb més facilitat els fenòmens que passin cap al sud o a la mateixa façana marítima i, en aquest sentit, serà fàcil poder seguir els temporals de mar des d’aquest punt de contacte. nou canal de WhatsApp Vols rebre cada dia la previsió del temps per WhatsApp? El Tibidabo, un 360 º per veure-ho gairebé tot betevé recupera també una imatge històrica: la vista des de Collserola , una vista perduda fa uns anys amb el deteriorament de l’envellida càmera que hi ha a la torre de comunicacions de Collserola. Ara, amb la nova ubicació al Parc d’Atraccions del Tibidabo, es manté la vista cap a la ciutat , però també podrem veure el que passa fins i tot a la basílica del Tibidabo . En aquest sentit, pot ser una gran eina en moments en què la neu pugui fer acte de presència a la part més alta de la ciutat. La càmera permet també veure què passa en alguns punts del Vallès i també ens deixarà veure si ha nevat al Montseny o el creixement de les nuvolades del nord-est, també visibles des de Montjuïc. La càmera situada al Castell de Montjuïc continuarà oferint la seva preciosa panoràmica de mar a muntanya des d’una talaia privilegiada que permet especialment la vista cap al nord. articles.body: (ACN/Redacció) El president d’Enraona Teatre i exdirector de la desapareguda i emblemàtica companyia de teatre Dagoll Dagom, Joan Lluís Bozzo, s’endinsa de nou en l’ imaginari de Dagoll Dagom amb Les veles s’inflaran . L’espectacle tindrà més de 30 artistes i inclourà música i personatges de títols emblemàtics com Mar i cel, Flor de nit, Nit de Sant Joan, Antaviana i El Mikado. Les veles s’inflaran s’estrenarà el 15 de novembre al teatre El Progrés de Martorell . Preveu fer gira per Catalunya i asseguren que la idea és aterrar a Barcelona la temporada vinent . També et pot interessar ‘Mar i cel’ plega veles amb entrades exhaurides i 10 minuts d’aplaudiments Lluís Cruz Berasategui Queralt Gómez Cuberes 2 minuts de lectura Militància en català Joan Lluís Bozzo, retirat de la direcció, signa l’ única escena de text del muntatge : “Cosa que em pensava que no faria mai més, però estic molt content”, ha dit. Així, ha destacat que una de les finalitats de la companyia és la “militància del teatre en català” . Així mateix, Bozzo ha assenyalat que la previsió és incorporar al muntatge música en directe i que utilitzaran moltes de les peces de vestuari de Dagoll Dagom. Estarà dirigit per Mariona Bosch de la Cruz i Mariona Bosch Nuri, mentre que la direcció coreogràfica va a càrrec de Mimi Carbó. També et pot interessar Joan Lluís Bozzo torna al teatre amb una obra sobre salut mental i adolescents Clara Vera Colina 3 minuts de lectura Enraona Teatre, més enllà del teatre Joan Lluís Bozzo va ser el director artístic de la coneguda companyia Dagoll Dagom durant quatre dècades, fins que va jubilar-se. El 2024 va fundar Enraona Teatre , amb què va estrenar el muntatge Pots ser tu, puc ser jo sobre salut mental en l’adolescència. La companyia entén el teatre com una eina social, terapèutica, pedagògica i inclusiva.
